structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: Power and data-center footprint can control a scarce physical input to AI compute deployment.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: Contracted hyperscaler demand supports utilization, but concentrated customer exposure and phased execution create binary schedule risk.

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: Compute demand is robust, but hyperscalers can self-build or source from competing infrastructure providers.

discovery-weak-signals.name: hyperscaler AI infrastructure demand
discovery-weak-signals.basis: A named multi-year customer contract materially strengthens evidence that IREN's power-and-data-center footprint can convert into AI cloud demand.

adversarial-red-team.name: financingRisk
adversarial-red-team.basis: Large equipment and infrastructure commitments create substantial capital requirements before full revenue conversion.

adversarial-red-team.name: concentrationRisk
adversarial-red-team.basis: A very large named customer contract can make execution and renewal outcomes disproportionately important.

adversarial-red-team.name: confidenceInflation
adversarial-red-team.basis: Contract value and annualized run-rate should not be treated as present revenue or profit before commissioning.

expectations-execution.name: contract conversion
expectations-execution.basis: Large contracted demand is positive, but value realization depends on financing, procurement, construction, energization and GPU deployment occurring on schedule.

items.risk: The contract requires large-scale phased delivery and depends on infrastructure/GPU commissioning; contract value is not equivalent to recognized revenue or profit.

Customer concentration reduces resilience if a major contract is modified or not renewed.
